clue.text: Roman officers run section badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the words run section are put into a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: Legionary commanders are making a poor job of running their unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A centurion commanded a century, roughly a hundred soldiers, in the Roman army, so these are Roman officers.

clue.text: Care to let go of a wife's hands?

indicators.note: the word Care is made to release one of its letters, the a named next to it

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife, the 's linking it to what follows

explanation.surface: A question about whether to stop holding your spouse's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to let go of a' takes the A out of CARE, leaving CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands is an old word for workers, especially sailors, and a ship's crew is its body of hands.

clue.text: Forgotten knight returned holding nag's tail

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: the elected word holds the next piece inside it, as a container

parts.note: an MP returned at an election has been elected

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of nag

explanation.surface: A knight comes home riding a horse, having been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like a reversal signal, but it means voted in, ELECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neglected has been overlooked or left uncared for, much as a forgotten thing is.

clue.text: Leading group in distress

parts.note: a side that is leading is up, ahead in the score
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: The band at the top of the bill is in some trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset is troubled or distraught, the state of a person in distress.

clue.text: Fashionable drink in outskirts of Stroud as an alternative

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: this second in places the drink inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters of Stroud

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A trendy drink on the edge of Stroud, a Gloucestershire town, offered in place of something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something, which is what an alternative is.

clue.text: United Nations overturned sanction for type of weapon?

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: to sanction is to approve or clear something

explanation.surface: The UN reverses its sanction on a kind of weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanction' suggests a penalty, but here it is the verb meaning approve.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear bomb is one kind of weapon; the question mark marks the answer as an adjective describing a type.

clue.text: Island offering cereal crop — for the ears

indicators.note: something meant for the ears is heard, not read, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: barley is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: An island that grows a grain crop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BARLEY and BALI sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island, famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Something to climb left out for snake

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is omitted

parts.note: a ladder is something you climb

explanation.surface: A climbing frame left behind for a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a kind of viper.

clue.text: In secret I'd developed rash

indicators.note: letters that have developed have changed form, so In secret I'd is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A skin rash appeared without anyone knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' reads as a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: An indiscreet act is careless and unguarded, much like a rash, hasty one.

clue.text: News chief's entertaining heads of government — enormous creeps

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the editor's letters hold the next ones

parts.note: a newspaper's chief is the editor, ED, and the 's gives ED'S

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hosting senior government figures, who are huge creeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeps' looks like a noun for unpleasant people but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to move slowly and cautiously, just as one creeps.

clue.text: Model seduced outside church? Victor did it

indicators.note: the reshaped letters sit outside the church abbreviation
to model is to shape, so the letters of seduced are reshaped

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A model seduced near a church, and a man called Victor was responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a name but means a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor has won, and to win is to succeed, so what a victor did was succeed.

clue.text: Beg to be in French outing?

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a treat is a special trip or outing

explanation.surface: Asking to be included in a trip to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or implore earnestly, a synonym for beg.

clue.text: Major half-trembles in English river

indicators.note: the half-word is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: half of the word trembles is its first four letters

explanation.surface: An army major shakes partly as he stands in an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like a rank but is the adjective meaning very great.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means very great or severe, a sense shared by major.

clue.text: Spells words

explanation.surface: A magician's incantations.
explanation.definitionFit: A term can be a fixed period, such as a school term, or a word or expression.

clue.text: Curious — being fine, I sat dance out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: the dance being out means its letters, with the others, are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone, being well, oddly decided to skip a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascinated person is gripped by interest, like a curious one keen to know more.

clue.text: Hesitated with female going to get changed

indicators.note: the female letter going means it is dropped

parts.note: to falter is to hesitate

explanation.surface: A man hesitated, then a woman left to get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered is a synonym for changed or modified.

clue.text: Release right priest before close of day

indicators.note: the priest comes before the evening in the answer

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
eve is an old word for evening, the close of the day

explanation.surface: A priest is freed in good time before nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone can mean to free them of a duty or burden, a sense of release.

clue.text: Animal runs over with energy — grass has come back

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the grass word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An animal dashes over, full of energy, after the grass has grown back.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer, so a kind of animal.

clue.text: Being sixteen, worried about Ecstasy

indicators.note: worried here means pulled about, so the letters of sixteen are jumbled

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old anxious about taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of existing, a synonym of existence.

clue.text: Scout did sleep, so every other character lies close

indicators.note: taking every other character means the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A Scout slept, snuggled up beside a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuddles up holds another tightly, lying close beside them.

clue.text: Expect attitude after drink

indicators.note: the attitude word goes after the drink word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Anticipating a posture after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or believe something likely, much as you expect it.

clue.text: Count winemaker's bottles spread out

indicators.note: the words bottle up, or contain, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: An aristocratic winemaker's bottles laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to undo strands, separating them out.

clue.text: Vain American embracing tennis player

indicators.note: the American letters embrace the player, holding her name inside

parts.note: US stands for American, of the United States
Monica Seles is a former world number one tennis player

explanation.surface: A conceited American hugging a tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like conceited but means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of fruitless, as in a vain attempt, means useless.

clue.text: Jog naked around centre of Margate

indicators.note: the naked word goes around the middle letter

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: the centre of Margate is its fourth, middle letter

explanation.surface: Running naked around the middle of Margate, a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' suggests running but means a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a light push, which is a nudge.

clue.text: 500 Royal Engineers put on ship's clothing

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
RE is the abbreviation for the British Army's Royal Engineers
SS, steamship, is the prefix in a ship's name

explanation.surface: Five hundred army engineers boarding a ship in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress as a noun means clothing in general, as in formal dress.

clue.text: Penny with object to give out

parts.note: to resent something is to object to it bitterly

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny refusing to hand things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To present prizes is to hand or give them out.

clue.text: Player making run in cricket

definitions.meaning: an actor in a film crowd scene with no lines
a run scored without the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.surface: A cricketer scoring a run.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a background actor and also a cricket run not credited to the batsman.

clue.text: Spare tyres cease to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to stop is to cease

explanation.surface: Spare wheels that won't stop going up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare tyres' is slang for rolls of belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots are pot bellies, and a spare tyre is a roll of fat round the waist.

clue.text: So upsetting for the peer, having lost power

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them over into a new order
the words for the peer lose one letter before the shuffle

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: This is so distressing for the lord, who has lost his influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost power' removes the P, leaving FORTHEEER to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: So and therefore both mean for that reason, introducing a consequence.

clue.text: Dance with zero taste? The contrary

indicators.note: the contrary order to zero with taste puts the taste first and zero after it

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A dance performed with no flair at all, or the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a Latin American ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Make hush money

parts.note: to do can mean to make, as in do a drawing
sh is the sound used to hush someone

explanation.surface: Paying someone to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make hush money' looks like a bribe but splits as make, hush and money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for cash or money.

clue.text: Bridge players requiring ID? It will make the press

parts.note: the four bridge players are North, East, West and South, N E W S
identity documents are papers

explanation.surface: Card players needing identification, which would get into the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The press means the newspaper industry collectively, the printed papers.
